assessment: The authors demonstrate that targeted memory reactivation (TMR) can enhance motor memory consolidation. TMR has mainly been used to strengthen declarative memories, and, on a neurophysiological level, TMR has been shown to strengthen oscillatory cross-frequency coupling. Here the authors extend previous findings into the motor domain and reveal that TMR strengthens motor memories and again, cross-frequency coupling of cardinal sleep oscillations, namely slow waves and spindles. Collectively, their findings provide additional evidence for the idea that the temporal precision of cross-frequency network coordination is critical for timed information transfer from short-term to long-term mnemonic storage.
